monument_name: Sundargāũ Sundar Mani Malika Mandira, western temple
anglicized_name: Sundargaon Sundar Mani Malika Mandira, western temple
name_devanagari: सुन्दर्गाउँ सुन्दर् मनि मलिक मन्दिर, पश्चिमी मन्दिर || JUM0350
description_en: The oracular temple in Sundargāũ is situated on a wooded terrace to the southwest of the village. Sundargāũ is located on the left bank of the Tilā Nadī. Adjacent to the east of the temple is another smaller oracular temple (JUM0351).The temple is oriented towards the northeast and constructed using roughly cut stones and mud mortar. The lower half of the walls is plastered with ochre earth, while the upper half is coated with kaolinite. The entrance to the temple is preceded by a large pole known asluga, which supports wooden sculptures. The interior of the temple is rectangular and divided into three sections. The first section serves as a vestibule, with a single pillar supporting the entablature of the facade. Devotees have placed stone and wooden statues in the vestibule, most of which depict individuals in a praying gesture (añjali mudrā). A door leads to the second empty room, and from there, another door provides access to the third room. Inside the third room, a small fireplace (kuṇḍaoragenā) is situated on the floor next to an altar consisting of three niches, likely constructed with stones and covered with earth.Old photographs indicate that the floor level of the temple used to be higher and has been lowered in the past few decades. Similarly, the original wooden roof has been replaced with corrugated metal sheets.Based on its current layout, the temple is believed to have been constructed in the 19th or early 20th century. However, two of the stone statues found at the site are likely older than the existing temple itself.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
